GEN.name: General Studies (Years 1-2)
GEN.description: The General Studies programme covers the foundational two years that every FCI student completes before choosing a specialisation. It builds the mathematical, programming, and systems-thinking skills that all computing graduates need — from discrete mathematics and physics through database design, networking, artificial intelligence fundamentals, and cyber security basics.
objectives: Build rigorous mathematical fluency (calculus, linear algebra, discrete structures, probability)
Introduce programming from first principles through to data structures and algorithms
Develop understanding of hardware from logic gates to computer architecture
Expose students to databases, networks, operating systems, and security before they specialise
Provide English language and professional communication foundations
careers: Any of the five specialist pathways: CS, AI, Cyber Security, Data Science, Software Engineering

CS.name: Computer Sciences
CS.description: The Computer Sciences department dives deep into the theory and practice of computing — algorithms, graphics, networks, security, compilers, vision, and cloud systems. Students follow a rigorous curriculum spanning classical CS theory and modern application areas such as machine learning, big data, and mobile computing.
objectives: Master core CS theory: algorithms, compilers, operating systems, and computer architecture
Apply AI, machine learning, and computer vision to real-world problems
Design and implement secure networked systems
Develop proficiency in graphics, HCI, and cloud/mobile platforms
Conduct and communicate technical research at a graduate-ready level
tools: Python · TensorFlow · OpenGL · Wireshark · Docker · Kubernetes · Java · C++

AI.name: Artificial Intelligence
AI.description: The Artificial Intelligence department trains students to build intelligent systems across the full AI stack — from theoretical foundations in automated reasoning and cognitive science, through deep learning, NLP, and robotics, to emerging areas such as speech processing, virtual/augmented reality, and autonomous agents.
objectives: Understand the theoretical foundations of AI: logic, reasoning, search, and learning
Implement and evaluate modern deep learning models (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers)
Build NLP pipelines for text understanding, generation, and translation
Design and program autonomous robotic and agent-based systems
Apply AI ethically with awareness of bias, transparency, and accountability
tools: Python · PyTorch · TensorFlow · ROS2 · Unity · Prolog · Hugging Face · OpenCV

CSCS.name: Cyber Security
CSCS.description: The Cyber Security department trains students to defend systems and networks against the full spectrum of digital threats. The curriculum spans cryptographic theory, penetration testing, digital forensics, risk management, cloud security, IoT security, and cyber warfare — teaching both offensive techniques (to understand attackers) and defensive strategies (to build resilient systems).
objectives: Master cryptographic foundations: symmetric, asymmetric, hash functions, and protocols
Conduct ethical hacking: reconnaissance, exploitation, forensics, and incident response
Apply risk frameworks (NIST, ISO 27001) to build and audit information security programmes
Secure web applications, networks, cloud platforms, and IoT deployments
Understand cyber law, policy, and the geopolitics of nation-state cyber operations
tools: Kali Linux · Metasploit · Wireshark · Nmap · Burp Suite · Splunk · AWS Security Hub · QEMU

ISDS.name: Information Systems & Data Science
ISDS.description: The Information Systems & Data Science department bridges computer science, statistics, and business intelligence. Students develop expertise across the full data pipeline — acquiring, storing, processing, and visualising data to extract actionable insights. The curriculum covers statistical modelling, machine learning, blockchain, time series, big data platforms, and BI tools.
objectives: Build statistical and probabilistic foundations for data-driven decision making
Design and query relational, NoSQL, and distributed data storage systems
Apply machine learning, data mining, and deep learning to large-scale datasets
Create interactive visualisations and BI dashboards for business stakeholders
Understand emerging technologies: blockchain, IoT data streams, and federated learning
tools: Python · pandas · scikit-learn · Spark · Hadoop · Tableau · Power BI · MongoDB · Kafka · SQL

SE.name: Software Engineering
SE.description: The Software Engineering department trains students to deliver software reliably and at scale. Beyond coding, students master the complete engineering discipline: requirements elicitation, architecture design, quality assurance, team coordination, security integration, and deployment. Advanced courses cover IoT software, big data systems, cloud and mobile platforms.
objectives: Elicit, specify, and validate software requirements to professional standards
Design robust software architectures (microservices, event-driven, layered patterns)
Apply rigorous testing strategies: TDD, mutation testing, automated test frameworks
Integrate security throughout the SDLC using DevSecOps practices
Manage software projects with Agile methodologies and professional toolchains
tools: Git · Docker · Jenkins · Jira · JUnit · SonarQube · Kubernetes · GitHub Actions · IntelliJ IDEA

CP101.name: Computer Programming (1)
CP101.description: First programming course — variables, conditionals, loops, functions, and arrays in a structured language. Students write, run, and debug small programs, building computational thinking from the ground up.

DS101.name: Discrete Structures
DS101.description: Logic, sets, relations, functions, proof techniques, graphs, and combinatorics. The mathematical backbone of computer science — nearly every theoretical topic in later courses depends on this material.

ENG101.name: English (1)
ENG101.description: Develops academic reading and writing in English, with a focus on comprehension, vocabulary in context, and structured paragraph writing. Prepares students for technical documentation and report writing.

ICS101.name: Introduction to Computer Science
ICS101.description: An entry-level tour of the discipline: what computers are, how they process data, the history of computing, binary representation, logic gates, and an introduction to problem-solving and algorithm thinking. Sets the language every subsequent course builds on.

MATH101.name: Math (1)
MATH101.description: Calculus and precalculus foundations: limits, derivatives, integration, sequences, and series. Essential mathematical fluency for algorithm analysis, signal processing, and AI courses in later years.

PHYS101.name: Physics
PHYS101.description: Classical mechanics, waves, optics, and an introduction to electricity and magnetism. Provides the physical intuition behind hardware, signals, and electronics studied in subsequent semesters.

DC102.name: Digital Circuitry
DC102.description: Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational and sequential circuits, flip-flops, registers, and counters. Bridges the gap between software abstraction and physical hardware reality.

DSTR102.name: Data Structures
DSTR102.description: Linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, hash tables, and graphs — with analysis of time and space complexity. One of the most important courses in the curriculum; the basis for algorithms and database courses.

ELEC102.name: Electronics
ELEC102.description: Electronic components (diodes, transistors, op-amps), circuit analysis, and basic signal theory. Background knowledge for hardware interfacing, IoT, and embedded systems courses.

ENGIT102.name: English for IT Professionals
ENGIT102.description: Technical English: reading IT documentation, writing specifications, presenting ideas in English, and understanding the vocabulary of software engineering and systems administration.

MATH102.name: Math (2)
MATH102.description: Continues from Math (1): multivariable calculus, linear algebra (vectors, matrices, eigenvalues), and differential equations. Linear algebra is foundational to machine learning and graphics in upper years.

TIS102.name: Technology of Information Systems
TIS102.description: Overview of how organisations use information systems: ERP, CRM, transaction processing, decision support, and the role of IT governance. Bridges computer science with business context.

AAD201.name: Algorithms Analysis and Design
AAD201.description: Algorithm correctness and complexity (Big-O, Omega, Theta), sorting algorithms, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, and NP-completeness. Core theory for every upper-year major.

CN201.name: Computer Networks
CN201.description: OSI and TCP/IP models, IP addressing, routing protocols, Ethernet, HTTP, DNS, and network security basics. The foundation for advanced networking and cyber security courses.

COS201.name: Computer Operating Systems
COS201.description: Process management, scheduling, memory management (paging, segmentation), file systems, I/O management, and concurrency (semaphores, monitors). Essential for systems programming and security.

DBS201.name: Database Systems
DBS201.description: Relational model, ER diagrams, SQL, normalisation (1NF–BCNF), transactions, concurrency control, and an introduction to NoSQL. Students design and query databases across every specialisation.

OR201.name: Operations Research
OR201.description: Optimisation techniques: linear programming, simplex method, transportation models, assignment problems, and network analysis. Used in scheduling, resource allocation, and AI planning.

STAT201.name: Statistics & Probability (1)
STAT201.description: Descriptive statistics, probability theory, distributions (binomial, Poisson, normal), expectation, hypothesis testing, and regression. The mathematical language of data science and machine learning.

BAI202.name: Artificial Intelligence (1)
BAI202.description: Classic AI: search algorithms (BFS, DFS, A*), knowledge representation, constraint satisfaction, and a first look at machine learning and expert systems. Gateway to the AI specialisation.

BCS202.name: Basics of Cyber Security
BCS202.description: Threat landscape, attack types (phishing, malware, MITM), basic cryptography, authentication, secure coding principles, and an introduction to risk management. Feeds into the Cyber Security specialisation.

CA202.name: Computer Architecture
CA202.description: CPU organisation, instruction set architecture, pipelining, cache memory, virtual memory, and I/O systems. Explains how software maps to hardware — foundational for CS and AI majors.

MS202.name: Modeling and Simulation
MS202.description: Mathematical modelling of systems, Monte Carlo simulation, queuing theory, and event-driven simulation. Supports data science, AI, and operations research in advanced years.

SAD202.name: System Analysis and Design
SAD202.description: Requirements engineering, UML diagrams, structured and object-oriented analysis, prototyping, and project scoping. Critical for software engineering and information systems majors.

SEF202.name: Software Engineering Fundamentals
SEF202.description: Software development life cycle, agile and waterfall methodologies, version control, software quality, and an introduction to testing and maintenance.

AI301.name: Machine and Deep Learning
AI301.description: Supervised and unsupervised learning, neural network architectures (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers), backpropagation, regularisation, and hands-on training with TensorFlow/PyTorch.

AI302.name: Principles of IOT
AI302.description: IoT ecosystem: sensors, actuators, embedded microcontrollers (Arduino, Raspberry Pi), communication protocols (MQTT, CoAP), cloud integration, and IoT data analytics.

AI303.name: Automated Reasoning
AI303.description: Logic programming (Prolog), constraint solving, SAT and SMT solvers, planning algorithms, and their applications in AI agents and verification systems.

AI304.name: Selected Topics in AI
AI304.description: Cutting-edge AI research: adversarial machine learning, explainable AI (XAI), federated learning, and recent breakthroughs in large language models and multimodal systems.

AI305.name: Report Writing Skills & Communication
AI305.description: Research writing for AI practitioners: structuring technical papers, citing literature, presenting experiments, and communicating model results to technical and non-technical audiences.
